label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
**To whoever is putting rubbish in my bin,**

I’m writing this to everyone on Aughrim Terrace because I don’t know who’s doing it, and I’m not interested in accusing the wrong person. But whoever you are, please stop using my bin.

I live at No. 14, and my grey bin has **14 painted in white on the lid**. Greenmount Bins charges by weight at 41 cent per kilo. My last bill was €63.20 for two months; it’s usually around €25. That extra cost isn’t mine to absorb, and I’m not paying for someone else’s rubbish.

The bin goes out on Tuesday night for collection Wednesday morning. When I got home at 3am last Wednesday, after work, the lid wouldn’t even close. There were three black bags in it that weren’t mine, including one with nappies. This hasn’t been a one-off: full bags have been turning up week after week for about a month. It’s not a few bits dropped in by mistake.

Someone mentioned seeing a car pull up on Tuesday evening, but didn’t see who it was. I also found a gas-bill envelope in one of the bags, but the name had been torn off and it only showed the terrace. I’m not putting that here to start a witch-hunt; I just want whoever’s responsible to know this has been noticed.

If you’re stuck and need help sorting your rubbish, ask me. I’ll tell you who to ring. It’s not hard to sort out properly. But putting full bags in a neighbour’s bin without asking—and leaving them with the bill—isn’t acceptable.

I work nights, so please don’t take a late hour as an invitation to use my bin or assume I won’t notice. I’m not looking for a row; I just want this to stop. If it keeps happening, I’ll start locking the bin with a padlock.

**Please stop using my bin. Simple as.**

**No. 14, Aughrim Terrace**
